houseRules.description: The Monk is a 100% house class (confirmed by owner): its level table, abilities, XP, skills, prohibitions and prefills all come from house rules, none from the PHB/DMG.

INT 'Bonus Spells 1st-4th'. Wizard only (confirmed by owner, not the Bard). Uses the same bonus-spell table as WIS, looked up with the INT score. Shown on wizard sheets and multi-classes containing a wizard.
WIS field labelled 'Mental Save' on the sheets. PHB Table 5 calls the WIS value 'Magical Defense Adjustment'; the sheet label is probably the same value renamed. Confirm.
'Melee Move' movement rate shown alongside Normal, Encumbered and Swimming.
Equipment tracked in two lists: Melee Encumbrance and Normal Encumbrance, each with its own total.
Sheet rows for Raised from Dead, Hasted and Unnatural Ageing (20 boxes each). Probably tallies rather than per-level values.

Sheets print 'Non Proficient/Related Penalty' as two values (e.g. -3/-2 on the Monk). PHB Table 34 gives the non-proficient weapon penalty per group (Warrior -2, Wizard -5, Priest -3, Rogue -3); the second ('related') value is not on that table.
No class loses its Constitution hit point bonus after name level. ALL classes receive the relevant CON bonus at ALL levels.

sheetVariations: No Hit Prob / Dmg Adj on the STR row.
No Adjusted AC sub-lines (Surprised, Shieldless, Rear, Natural); the area has an area-effects note instead.
Thief skills subset: Move Silently, Find Traps, Climb Walls, Hide in Shadows, Hear Noise.
Extra damage with proficient weapons: 1 point per 2 levels.

abilities.stunAndFatalBlow: With Open Hand a Monk may stun a humanoid opponent if the to-hit roll is exceeded by 5 or more, or a natural 20 is rolled (unless a 20 is required to hit). An opponent can only be affected once. Opponents are stunned for the remainder of that round and 1d4 additional rounds. Stunned victims suffer a loss of dexterity bonuses, -4 on AC, to hit and all saves, and are unable to cast spells.
abilities.dodgingMissiles: Daggers, axes, arrows and crossbow bolts can be dodged or knocked aside; machine-launched missiles and thrown boulders can be dodged but not knocked aside. Saving throw vs Petrification (DEX bonus applies), -1 for each magical plus of the missile. One missile per level per round can be dodged. -1 Move per missile avoided, and the Monk cannot attack or activate any other special abilities. Magic Missiles or similar spells cannot be dodged.
abilities.prohibitions: Cannot use flaming oil or poisons. Cannot turn or command undead.
abilities.qigong: The Monk's body counts as magical weapons for deciding which creatures may be hit (see the Qi column). This bonus does not apply to hit or damage rolls.
abilities.areaEffects: Against magical damaging spells or breath weapons where saving throws are allowed, the Monk sustains no damage if the save succeeds and only 50% of the total damage if it fails.

levelTable.notes: Qi is the magical-weapon equivalence for deciding which creatures can be hit (shown as +N). dmgRange is as printed on the sheet. Note: level 5 qi printed '+1', level 19 printed 'Any'.

druid.source: 2e PHB druid Granted Powers (text supplied by owner), paraphrased

grantedPowers.text: Saves as a priest, with a +2 bonus to all saving throws against fire or electrical attacks.
Speaks the secret druidic language in addition to any other tongues. Its vocabulary is limited to nature and natural events. Under the optional proficiency rules it does not use a proficiency slot.
Identifies plants, animals and pure water with perfect accuracy.
Passes through overgrown areas (thick thorn bushes, tangled vines, briar patches, etc.) without leaving a trail and at normal movement rate.

Can learn the languages of woodland creatures: one at 3rd level and one more for each level advanced above 3rd. Under the optional proficiency rules the druid chooses whether to spend a proficiency slot on these.
Immune to charm spells cast by woodland creatures (dryads, nixies, etc.).

Can shapechange into a reptile, bird or mammal up to three times per day; each of the three animal types can be used only once per day. Size ranges from a bullfrog or small bird up to a black bear. On assuming a new form the druid heals 10-60% (1d6 x 10%) of the damage he has suffered, rounding fractions down. Only normal, real-world animals in normal proportions, taking on all of the creature's characteristics (movement, abilities, AC, attacks, damage). Clothing and one item held in each hand become part of the new body and cannot be used until normal form resumes.

paladin.source: 2e PHB paladin special benefits (text supplied by owner), paraphrased

specialAbilities.name: Detect evil
specialAbilities.text: Detects evil intent up to 60 feet away by concentrating on a direction. Can be used as often as desired, but each attempt takes one round. Detects evil monsters and characters.

specialAbilities.name: Immunity to disease
specialAbilities.text: Immune to all forms of disease. Cursed afflictions such as lycanthropy and mummy rot are not diseases.

specialAbilities.name: Lay on hands
specialAbilities.text: Heals by laying on hands, restoring 2 hit points per experience level, to himself or another. Once per day.

specialAbilities.name: Cure disease
specialAbilities.text: Cures diseases of all sorts (not cursed afflictions such as lycanthropy), once per week for each five levels of experience: once per week at levels 1-5, twice at 6-10, and so on.

specialAbilities.name: Aura of protection
specialAbilities.text: Surrounded by a 10-foot-radius aura of protection. Within it, all summoned and specifically evil creatures suffer a -1 penalty to their attack rolls regardless of whom they attack. Affected creatures can spot the aura's source easily, even if the paladin is disguised.

specialAbilities.name: Holy sword
specialAbilities.text: A paladin using a holy sword projects a circle of power 10 feet in diameter while it is unsheathed and held. This dispels hostile magic of a level up to the paladin's experience level. The DM explains the sword's other powers if one is acquired.

specialAbilities.name: Turn undead and fiends
specialAbilities.text: From 3rd level turns undead and fiends as a cleric two levels lower (at 3rd level, as a 1st-level cleric).

specialAbilities.name: War horse
specialAbilities.text: May call for a war horse at 4th level or any time after. The steed need not be a horse and is decided by the DM. The paladin does not simply summon it: he must find it in a memorable way, usually by a quest.

specialAbilities.name: Priest spells
specialAbilities.text: Can cast priest spells from 9th level, only from the combat, divination, healing and protective spheres, under the priest's spell rules. Spell progression and casting level are on Table 17. No extra spells for high Wisdom. Cannot cast from clerical or druidical scrolls, and cannot use priest items unless they are allowed to the warrior group.

magicalItems.note: Arrows and bolts are not counted toward the weapon limit.
magicalItems.sheetCrossCheck: The Paladin sheet has numbered Magical Items 1-10, matching the limit of 10.

wealth.text: A paladin never retains wealth. He may keep only enough to support himself modestly, pay his henchmen, men-at-arms and servitors a reasonable rate, and build or maintain a small castle or keep (funds may be set aside for this). All excess must be donated to the church or another worthy cause, and can never be given to another player character or an NPC controlled by a player.
wealth.appHint: Treasure block: warn when a paladin's treasure exceeds what he can keep, and do not allow transfers to other player characters.

tithe.text: Must tithe 10% of all income (coins, jewels, magical items, wages, rewards or taxes), paid immediately, to a charitable religious institution of lawful good alignment that he serves.
tithe.appHint: Offer a 'tithe due' calculator on income entries.

conduct.followers: A paladin does not attract followers at 9th level or on building a castle, but may hire soldiers and specialists, who must be lawful good in comportment.
conduct.henchmen: Employs only lawful good henchmen (or those who act that way when alignment is unknown). Cooperates with others of different alignment only while they behave, and will not abide those who commit evil or unrighteous acts. Non-evil thieves sincerely trying to reform can be tolerated. Stealth in a good cause is acceptable only as a last resort.

speciesEnemy.text: Species Enemy (+4 to hit / -4 reaction adjustment).

skillNotes: Hide in Shadows and Move Silently are halved if attempted in non-natural surroundings (e.g. crypt, city streets).
These skills are not possible in armour heavier than studded leather.
Wearing studded leather or lighter armour, a ranger can attack with two weapons with no penalty.

armourLimitForSkills.rule: Hide in Shadows and Move Silently are not possible in armour heavier than studded leather; two-weapon fighting without penalty needs studded leather or lighter.
armourLimitForSkills.byArmourClass: armour with AC lower than 7 is heavier than studded leather; ring mail (AC 7) also counts as heavier by owner ruling
armourLimitForSkills.source: Table 46 AC values (comparison by AC, as used for the bard); owner to confirm that AC is the right test for rangers.

ruling.text: Ring mail counts as heavier than studded leather.
ruling.why: Ring mail has the same AC as studded leather (7) but weighs more (30 lb against 25 lb), so a tie on AC is broken by treating ring mail as the heavier armour.

abilities.text: 5% chance per level to identify the general purpose and function of any magical item.

scrollUse.effectOnMisread: The scroll is read incorrectly and the spell's effect is reversed or goes wrong, almost always to the detriment of the thief and party. Exact effect decided by the DM.
scrollUse.sheetWording: Can read Priest scrolls at 10th Level - 25% chance failure
scrollUse.sheetWordingStatus: incomplete: should say magical and priest scrolls

classRecipes.description: Which blocks each class shows on a sheet. A multi-class character gets the union of its classes' blocks, one XP column and one HP-per-level row per class. Derived from the 20 provided sheets; they match this union rule.

bard.legacySheetNote: Old Bard sheet printed an INT Bonus Spells row; removed (INT bonus spells are Wizard only).

notes: Only the single-class Fighter sheet shows 'Specialized Weapons' and the point-blank (PB +2) range band; multi-class sheets with a fighter component omit both. Weapon specialisation is single-class Fighter only (confirmed by owner).
Paladin and Ranger sheets show no bonus-spell rows by design: they never gain bonus spells from WIS or INT (confirmed by owner).
Cleric/Ranger and Druid/Ranger sheets show the Ranger skills block next to the cleric/druid blocks; Cleric multi-classes add Turn Undead; Druid multi-classes add Granted Powers.
WIS bonus spells row appears on any sheet with a cleric or druid component; INT bonus spells row only where a wizard is a component (not the bard).

int.table: uses the WIS bonus-spell table, looked up with the INT score
int.note: Wizard only (confirmed by owner). The Bard sheet's INT bonus-spell row is not part of the rule and should not appear on the new Bard PDF.

bonusSpells.note: Paladins and Rangers never gain bonus spells from WIS or INT, so their sheets have no bonus-spell rows. A multi-class character gets a bonus-spell row for each casting class that qualifies.

conBonusAllLevels.overrides: The core rule that no class gains Constitution hit point bonuses after name level (9th for warriors, clerics and druids, 10th for mages).
conBonusAllLevels.meaning: Each class keeps using the CON hit point adjustment its normal rules give it: the +2 per die cap for non-warriors, and the warrior-only parenthetical bonus for fighters, paladins and rangers.

afterNameLevel.rule: After name level a character gains a flat number of hit points per level (3 for warriors, 2 for druids). The CON bonus is added to that gain once per level.
afterNameLevel.example: A 12th-level fighter with CON 17 (+3 for warriors) gains 3 + 3 = 6 hit points per level.

conBonusAllLevels.coreRuleReference: rules-core.json classes: hitPointsAfterNameLevel.conBonusApplies is the core value (false).
